title: Memory pricing splits: DRAM contracts climb while NAND spot slides
summary: TrendForce expects PC DRAM contract prices to rise 13-18% in the fourth quarter and client SSD prices by less than 5%, after notebook shipments fell 15.8% sequentially in the third quarter. Suppliers are steering capacity to high-bandwidth memory, server DRAM and enterprise SSDs, leaving module makers short: 16Gb DDR5 contract prices are more than 500% higher year on year, while NAND spot has dropped roughly 20% since mid-October. Some producers say capacity is booked into 2028.
